sections.text: ## The Big Picture

metadata.title: Temperate Tree Species: Oak, Maple, Beech, Ash, Birch, Conifer Families

sections.text: Temperate forest trees divide cleanly into two anatomical kingdoms (gymnosperms and angiosperms) and then into major families that share wood anatomy, ecology, and timber characteristics. This guide covers the principal species groups of North American and European temperate forests with identifiable traits and wood properties.

sections.text: ## Section 1 — Gymnosperm vs. Angiosperm Wood Anatomy

metadata.title: Temperate Tree Species: Oak, Maple, Beech, Ash, Birch, Conifer Families

sections.text:
| Feature | Gymnosperm (Softwood) | Angiosperm (Hardwood) |
|---------|----------------------|----------------------|
| Water transport | Tracheids (bordered pits) | Vessels (perforated plates) |
| Mechanical support | Same tracheids | Separate fibers (libriform) |
| Ray width | Uniseriate (1 cell wide) mostly | Variable: 1 to 30+ cells wide |
| Resin canals | Present (Pinus, Picea, Larix) | Absent (except traumatic in some) |
| Ring visibility | Clear (density contrast EW/LW) | Variable (ring-porous vs. diffuse) |
| Machining | Easier; less dulling | Harder; vessel tearing an issue |
| Drying | Generally faster; less checking | Many species prone to degrade |

| Property | Red Oak | White Oak |

sections.text: Economically dominant in the eastern North American hardwood market; all maples are diffuse-porous.

metadata.title: Temperate Tree Species: Oak, Maple, Beech, Ash, Birch, Conifer Families

sections.text:
**Sugar maple special properties:**
- Curly, bird's-eye, and quilted figure forms — premium market value
- Sapwood is cream-white with almost no heartwood discoloration — favored for flooring
- Very high silica content → dulls cutting edges faster than most species

sections.text: ## Section 4 — Beeches (Fagus, Fagaceae)

metadata.title: Temperate Tree Species: Oak, Maple, Beech, Ash, Birch, Conifer Families

sections.text: *Fagus sylvatica* (European beech) and *F. grandifolia* (American beech) are structurally similar:

metadata.title: Temperate Tree Species: Oak, Maple, Beech, Ash, Birch, Conifer Families

sections.text:
| Property | European Beech | American Beech |
|----------|---------------|----------------|
| Janka hardness | ~1300 lbf | ~1300 lbf |
| Density (air-dry) | ~720 kg/m³ | ~740 kg/m³ |
| Ring-porous? | No — diffuse-porous | No — diffuse-porous |
| Rays | Very large, multiseriate | Large |
| Shrinkage | High (T: 11.8%, R: 5.8%) | High (T: 11.9%) |
| Durability | Class 5 (not durable) | Class 5 |
| Key uses | Furniture, plywood, turned ware | Furniture frames, veneer |

metadata.title: Temperate Tree Species: Oak, Maple, Beech, Ash, Birch, Conifer Families

sections.text: **Beech ecology note:** American beech is highly shade-tolerant and a persistent late-seral dominant in the Great Lakes / Appalachian region. It reproduces vegetatively by root sprouts, creating dense clonal groves. Currently devastated by Beech Bark Disease (BBD) — *Nectria* fungus introduced by European beech scale.

sections.text: ## Section 5 — Ashes (Fraxinus, Oleaceae)

metadata.title: Temperate Tree Species: Oak, Maple, Beech, Ash, Birch, Conifer Families

sections.text: Ashes are ring-porous, with large earlywood vessel rings and diffuse latewood fibers.

metadata.title: Temperate Tree Species: Oak, Maple, Beech, Ash, Birch, Conifer Families

sections.text:
| Property | White Ash | Black Ash | European Ash |
|----------|-----------|-----------|--------------|
| Janka hardness | 1320 lbf | 850 lbf | ~1260 lbf |
| Density | ~660 kg/m³ | ~540 kg/m³ | ~720 kg/m³ |
| Toughness | Very high | High | Very high |
| Key uses | Tool handles, baseball bats, oars | Basket splints, furniture | Sports equipment, furniture |

metadata.title: Temperate Tree Species: Oak, Maple, Beech, Ash, Birch, Conifer Families

sections.text: **Ash toughness:** Ash has exceptionally high energy absorption before failure — the reason for tool handles, hockey sticks, oars, and historically in bow-making. The ring-porous structure with pronounced latewood bands contributes to this.

metadata.title: Temperate Tree Species: Oak, Maple, Beech, Ash, Birch, Conifer Families

sections.text: **Emerald Ash Borer (EAB):** *Agrilus planipennis* (introduced from Asia, first detected Michigan 2002) has killed billions of ash trees across North America and is now established in Europe. Effectively eliminates *Fraxinus* from affected stands unless treated annually. A genuinely catastrophic ecological event comparable to chestnut blight.

sections.text: ## Section 6 — Birches (Betula, Betulaceae)

metadata.title: Temperate Tree Species: Oak, Maple, Beech, Ash, Birch, Conifer Families

sections.text: Birches are diffuse-porous pioneers with short-lived dominance after disturbance.

metadata.title: Temperate Tree Species: Oak, Maple, Beech, Ash, Birch, Conifer Families

sections.text:
| Species | Notes | Wood Use |
|---------|-------|----------|
| *B. papyrifera* (Paper birch) | White bark; N. American pioneer; very short-lived (70–80 yr) | Pulp, plywood, veneer, turned goods |
| *B. alleghaniensis* (Yellow birch) | Shade tolerant; long-lived; cherry-like figure | Furniture, cabinetry, flooring |
| *B. pendula* (Silver birch EU) | Short-lived; pioneer; thin white bark | Ply, pulp; important culturally (Finland, Russia) |
| *B. lenta* (Sweet birch) | Methyl salicylate scent; dense (820 kg/m³) | Premium furniture; flooring |

metadata.title: Temperate Tree Species: Oak, Maple, Beech, Ash, Birch, Conifer Families

sections.text: **Alnus (Alder)** in the same family: the nitrogen fixer. *A. rubra* (red alder, Pacific NW) is an actinorhizal species that fixes atmospheric N at up to 60–130 kg N/ha/yr through Frankia symbiosis. Ecologically critical in riparian zones and early post-disturbance succession.
